title: Networking basics
summary: What happens between a browser and a server: DNS, TCP and UDP, HTTP semantics, push channels, proxies and CDNs.

questions.prompt: What does DNS do when a browser opens example.com?
options: Translates the name into an IP address the client can connect to

questions.prompt: A live video call would rather drop a late frame than wait for it to be resent. Which transport fits?
Which HTTP method is defined as idempotent, so repeating the same request has the same effect as sending it once?
A POST successfully creates a new order. Which status code fits best?
A dashboard needs live updates from the server, and the browser never sends messages back over that channel. Which fits most simply?
What does a reverse proxy sit in front of?
options: Your servers, accepting client traffic on their behalf (TLS, routing, load balancing)
Clients, hiding them from the internet

questions.prompt: True or false: a CDN mainly helps by serving cacheable content (images, scripts, video) from locations close to users.
